decisions.reason: The quota remains 100 approved clips; the same-message variation counting rule and lifecycle resumption are already represented, while Lead Clipper advancement adds no further quota change.
The Lead Clipper advancement decision does not change which source videos or footage may be used.
Mastering the new approach is a prerequisite for future Lead Clipper advancement, not a change to the current clipper qualification process.
The source decision does not alter publication eligibility, destination, cadence, captioning, tagging, or reporting instructions.
The mention of shorter clip styles does not establish a replacement duration range, and the resulting same-message value uncertainty is already represented by the candidate's AMBIGUOUS Event.
The planned hook training and advancement prerequisite do not replace the existing requirement to select strong source moments or establish a concrete new moment-selection rule.
Future advancement of multiple clippers does not presently transfer approval authority or change the rule that only approved clips may be published.
Shorter production styles and Lead Clipper advancement do not revoke or modify the requirement that each clip deliver a complete standalone lesson, story, or point.
The source decision contains no change to caption color, font, effects, lettering, or position.
The new production approach and Lead Clipper pathway do not change the existing clean and simple editing constraints.
The source decision does not change the submission channel, folder configuration, deadline, batch size, or review-link workflow.
The Lead Clipper scaling and advancement prerequisite do not change the requirement to remove distracting wind noise.
